utility_name: Ameren Illinois Company d/b/a Ameren Illinois
rule_summary: Follows ICC/CEJA state default for net metering caps, aggregate cap, and interconnection levels. Deviation is the utility-specific DG/Smart Inverter Rebate schedule, which is tiered by rate class and explicitly covers storage inverters.
storage_specific_notes: DG/Smart Inverter Rebate: DS-1 & DS-2 (residential/small commercial) = $300/kW-DC for solar inverters, $300/kWh for storage inverters. utility_name: Union Electric Company d/b/a Ameren Missouri
rule_summary: Follows MoPSC state-default 100 kW cap, 5% aggregate cap, and 20 CSR 4240-20.065 interconnection process. Deviation is the utility's specific Rider NM billing mechanic: monthly exports credited at retail-adjacent net metering rate, but an ANNUAL true-up (reported by third parties as occurring in the customer's anniversary billing cycle) settles any remaining banked credit at the utility's Commission-filed avoided-cost/cogeneration rate rather than carrying it forward -- a materially different economic outcome than a pure monthly-rollover reading of the state rule. Reported approximate figures (not independently verified against a current Ameren Missouri tariff sheet): retail-adjacent monthly credit ~$0.115-0.13/kWh; year-end avoided-cost settlement ~$0.03-0.04/kWh.
storage_specific_notes: Storage-specific interconnection treatment not independently confirmed; Ameren Missouri's net metering tariff (Rider NM) predates widespread residential storage and does not appear to separately address battery grid-charging or non-export configurations in public-facing materials reviewed

rule_summary: Municipal utility not regulated by MoPSC; City Utilities sets its own net metering policy via municipal governance, though it mirrors the state's 100 kW cap. Offers its own solar rebate program in addition to net metering (rebate value not independently confirmed in this pass).

Municipal utility not regulated by MoPSC; Columbia sets its own net metering ordinance. Mirrors the state's 100 kW cap but pays a two-tier rate: retail rate to offset same-period consumption, then a much lower avoided-cost rate (~2-4 cents/kWh) for any net excess beyond monthly consumption -- a steeper reversion than reading MoPSC's 20 CSR 4240-20.065 alone would suggest. City purchases the customer's RECs as part of the net metering agreement (customer may instead elect to keep RECs and be paid at the avoided average energy market price at the Columbia pricing node in lieu of retail-rate netting). City also runs its own DG rebate schedule: $375-$625/kW for the first 10 kW, $300-$500/kW for kW 10-50, $150-$250/kW for kW 50-100.
storage_specific_notes: REC election is a key structural choice: keeping RECs switches the customer off retail-rate netting and onto avoided-cost LMP pricing at the Columbia node -- a storage/export economics factor not present in most other MO utilities reviewed

rule_summary: Municipal utility not regulated by MoPSC (governed instead by Independence City Council ordinance); voluntarily implements a policy that substantively mirrors RSMo 386.890 -- 100 kW cap, 1:1 retail rate net metering, and no-fee interconnection for systems <=10 kW. Because it is not an MoPSC-jurisdictional "electrical corporation," IPL is not legally bound by 386.890/20 CSR 4240-20.065 and could change terms via city ordinance without a PSC docket.

Cooperative -- statutorily covered by Act 464/278 net metering but administers its own tariff. For facilities interconnected after the 9/29/2024 cutoff, energy consumed from the co-op is billed at standard retail rate while exported energy is credited at avoided cost of energy based on the PRIOR YEAR's rate filed with APSC (a one-year-lagged avoided-cost figure, distinct from Entergy/SWEPCO's LMP-based approach). Unused credits roll over month to month and do not expire (explicit indefinite rollover, more generous than the state row's "not independently confirmed" default). A one-time administrative/interconnection fee applies to all net-metering submissions.

Municipally-owned utility (Ordinance No. 9329, adopted 2/8/2021) not under APSC jurisdiction; net metering/DG rules set independently by city ordinance. Uses a DUAL-METER configuration (separate meters for consumption and generation) rather than a single bidirectional net meter, with generation credited at Avoided Cost -- functionally closer to a buy-all/sell-all arrangement than true netting, a materially different economic structure than the APSC-jurisdictional utilities in this cluster. System size cap and full rate schedule not independently confirmed in this pass.
storage_specific_notes: Dual-meter/avoided-cost billing structure is a meaningful design consideration for battery-plus-solar economics -- self-consumption of stored solar may not net against grid draw the way it would under single-meter netting; needs direct verification against the ordinance text

rule_summary: Follows LPSC state default (General Order 9-19-2019): pre-2020 grandfathered 1:1 for 15 years, post-2019 avoided cost. No utility-specific deviation independently confirmed in this pass beyond its own published Avoided Cost rate (see LPSC's annual "Avoided Cost Rate by Electric Utility" document for the current figure).

CRITICAL: Entergy New Orleans is regulated by the NEW ORLEANS CITY COUNCIL, not the LPSC -- a wholly separate jurisdiction. The City Council adopted its own net-metering rules in May 2007, similar in structure to (but administered independently of) the LPSC's rules: residential systems up to 25 kW, commercial/agricultural up to 300 kW. Because New Orleans regulates its own utility, the September 2019 LPSC order that moved the rest of Louisiana to avoided-cost net billing for post-2019 interconnections did NOT automatically apply here -- New Orleans customers were reported (as of the 2019 LPSC change) to still have retail net metering available, making Entergy New Orleans a materially more favorable jurisdiction within the same corporate family than Entergy Louisiana. Current City Council net metering docket status and whether it has since moved to a similar avoided-cost structure was NOT independently confirmed in this pass -- treat as a high-priority gap given the economic significance.

Follows LPSC state default (General Order 9-19-2019/Docket R-33929) for the grandfathering cutoff and avoided-cost successor. No utility-specific deviation independently confirmed beyond its own published Avoided Cost rate.

Municipal utility -- LPSC does not regulate municipal utilities in Louisiana, so LUS's net metering program is set independently under its own board-approved rate structure and interconnection standards, not the LPSC General Order. LUS has a documented history of rate-structure volatility: it created a new (less favorable, colloquially called a "solar tax") rate structure for net-metered customers, then reversed course and restored its prior "smart solar" policy after public pushback (per Southern Alliance for Clean Energy reporting) -- flag for customers as a jurisdiction where terms have changed via local ordinance/board action rather than a formal PSC docket, and could change again.

Deviation is DEMCO's own published Avoided Energy Cost rate, updated annually each March based on wholesale-supplier-provided data: $0.02638/kWh effective March 1, 2025 - February 28, 2026.

rule_summary: Electric cooperative -- per MS H.B. 1139 (2016), the MPSC can require co-ops to offer net metering but CANNOT set the compensation/credit level; cooperatives may adopt the state net metering rule voluntarily or file their own independent standards. This is a major structural gap: roughly 57% of Mississippi ratepayers (co-op and municipal customers) are NOT bound by the MPSC's Chapter 03 Net Metering Rule caps, adders, or credit mechanics described in the state row. Coast Electric offers its own "Cooperative Solar"/net metering rate plan and REQUIRES panels be installed by a Mississippi-registered solar contractor -- self-installed systems are not permitted to interconnect (a notable design constraint not present in the IOU rules). Full rate schedule, system size cap, and credit basis not independently confirmed in this pass.
storage_specific_notes: Self-install prohibition is a hard eligibility gate specific to this cooperative -- relevant for any DIY or non-licensed-installer project pathway

rule_summary: CRITICAL DISTINCTION reinforced at the utility level: Entergy Texas is the vertically-integrated, PUCT-regulated, MISO-connected utility that the "Texas has no statewide net metering mandate" state-row caveat is actually ABOUT -- this is the one Texas utility where the limited PUCT net-metering rule (16 TAC 25.242) actually applies, because Entergy Texas is not unbundled/deregulated like ERCOT-area TDUs. Offers net metering under Schedule SQF (Option 2C, for qualifying renewable facilities <=50 kW AC where the interconnection agreement was initiated on/after 11/29/2017): customer billed for all energy supplied by the utility, and credited at Avoided Cost (calculated separately for on-peak/off-peak) for all energy exported. As of June 2023, all interconnection applications must be submitted through Entergy's online portal -- paper/manual applications no longer accepted.
export_credit_value: Avoided cost, calculated separately for on-peak and off-peak periods per Entergy Texas' annual PUCT avoided-cost filing (exact current cents/kWh not independently confirmed in this pass)
